facts.label: Source-by-source assessment
facts.text: - Entity and perimeter. The registrant is a single legal entity filing consolidated statements. Note 1 describes it as an "externally managed, non-diversified, closed-end management investment company" with "various wholly-owned subsidiaries, including special-purpose financing subsidiaries" (10-Q Q3 2026 page:67). The adviser is FS/KKR Advisor, LLC (10-K FY2025 page:4: "We are managed by FS/KKR Advisor, LLC"). Borrowings of the financing subsidiaries count as the Company's: "Borrowings of each of the Company’s wholly-owned, special-purpose financing subsidiaries are considered borrowings of the Company" (10-Q Q3 2026 page:113). No separate issuer, guarantor or restricted/unrestricted group is named in the sources read; the notes and credit-facility names (Callowhill, Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility, CLO-2, CLO-3) are borrowing vehicles inside the consolidated perimeter. - Original authority. The 10-K and 10-Qs are filed statements and control their facts. The three earnings releases are management presentations of the same quarters and carry non-GAAP measures (adjusted net investment income, net debt); they are attributed supporting claims and cannot override the filings. Where the release and the 10-Q show the same item they agree on the points sampled (net asset value per share $18.28 and total assets $11,695 in both the Q3 release pages 8 and 9 and the Q3 10-Q pages 2 and 3). - Periods and basis. Current period Q3 2026 is covered by the Q3 10-Q (three and nine months ended September 30, 2026) and the Q3 release. The prior period FY2025 is covered by the 10-K and by the December 31, 2025 comparative column in each 2026 10-Q (for example 10-Q Q3 2026 page:2, "Total assets $ 11,695 $ 13,729"). The Q1 and Q2 10-Qs and releases provide the intermediate quarters for a discrete Q1, Q2, Q3 view; the Q2 10-Q gives six-month and the Q3 10-Q nine-month cumulative columns, so quarter versus year-to-date must stay labelled. All amounts are USD millions unless marked; the senior revolver also holds euro, sterling and Australian dollar borrowings translated to USD (10-Q Q3 2026 page:110, footnote 4). - Version relationships. Each filing is the original for its period. No amendments (10-K/A, 10-Q/A) are in the pack. The pack does not hold any executed indenture, credit agreement, purchase agreement or supplement, so no base-versus-amendment question arises. - Debt and liquidity evidence located. Note 9 lists every financing arrangement with rate, amount outstanding, amount available and maturity, and gives the total: "Total $ 6,487 $ 3,197" including the $150 convertible preferred (10-Q Q3 2026 page:110). The senior revolver availability is stated net of standby letters of credit: "As of September 30, 2026, $50 of such letters of credit have been issued" (page:110). A December 31, 2025 table is on page:111. The 10-K carries the full note (10-K FY2025 page:259 onward, with the indenture descriptions on pages 274 to 276). Liquidity text, unfunded commitments and the asset coverage discussion are on 10-Q Q3 2026 pages 141 to 143; the 10-K equivalent is on page:144. - Covenant evidence located. The only compliance statement is generic: "The Company was in compliance with all covenants required by its financing arrangements as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025" (10-Q Q3 2026 page:113). The 10-K says the covenants "require us and our subsidiaries to, among other things, maintain certain financial ratios, including asset coverage and minimum stockholders’ equity" (10-K FY2025 page:93) without printing a threshold. The statutory asset coverage test is quantified in the 10-Q: coverage on senior securities representing indebtedness of 179% and on senior securities that are stock of 177%, against a 150% requirement (page:109 and pages 142 to 143). - Subsequent events and the cutoff. All seven sources were filed on or before 2026-11-05, so nothing postdates the cutoff. The Q3 10-Q and Q3 release were filed on the as-of date itself. Subsequent events are in the 10-Q Q3 2026 Note 13 (page:123) and release page:2: repurchases from October 1 through October 30, 2026, a declared fourth quarter distribution, a declared special distribution and a declared preferred dividend. Future payment dates in those items are declared terms, not events after the cutoff. - Transaction and ownership evidence. The 2026 capital actions are documented: the May release announces a $150 million convertible preferred from a KKR subsidiary, a $150 million tender offer, a $300 million repurchase program and a 50% incentive fee waiver (EX-99.1 Q1 2026 pages 2 and 3); the Q3 10-Q share transactions note records the preferred issue on June 29, 2026 to KKR Alternative Assets L.P. (page:74) and the $900 principal 7.500% Notes due 2031 issued June 8, 2026 appear in the Q2 10-Q (page:95) and the Q3 note table. Governing documents (purchase agreement, advisory agreement) are referenced but not supplied. - Joint venture. Credit Opportunities Partners JV, LLC is a 50/50 voting joint venture with South Carolina Retirement Systems Group Trust; the 10-Q gives selected balance sheet and income data (10-Q Q3 2026 page:94), including the joint venture's own debt, which is not the issuer's borrowing. The venture's full statements are not supplied.

facts.label: Conflicts, definitional differences and extraction cautions
facts.text: - Cash basis changed. The Q2 release nets "Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and foreign currency $ (109 )" in net debt (EX-99.1 Q2 2026 page:10), with restricted cash defined as "cash collateral required to be posted pursuant to the Company’s derivative contracts" (page:12). The Q3 release nets "Cash, cash equivalents, and foreign currency ($111)" (EX-99.1 Q3 2026 page:9), while the Q3 balance sheet shows "Restricted cash 61" separately (10-Q Q3 2026 page:2). The Q3 cash flow statement ends at "$ 172" including "restricted cash of $61" (page:5). The reported net debt-to-equity ratios (122% for Q2, 125% for Q3) are therefore not on an identical cash basis. Downstream modules must label which cash they use; CP-0 does not restate. - Three debt figures. The Q3 balance sheet shows "Debt (net of deferred financing costs and discount of $46 and $45, respectively) 6,231" (10-Q page:2), the Q3 release shows "Debt outstanding (principal) $6,337" (release page:9), and Note 9 totals "$ 6,487" including the convertible preferred (page:110). Footnote 7 on page:110 identifies hedge-accounting carrying adjustments on four notes. The differences are of basis (carrying versus principal versus including preferred); CP-0 does not reconcile them, and CP-1 must carry the basis with each figure. - Interest rate bases differ. The Q3 release quotes a "weighted average stated interest rate on borrowings was 5.57%" (release page:3) and the Q2 release a "weighted average effective interest rate (including the effect of non-usage fees) was 5.49%" (EX-99.1 Q2 2026 page:3); the Q3 10-Q gives 5.72% for the nine months including non-usage fees (page:113). These are different bases and periods, not a conflict in the filing. - Date labels. The Q1 release file name carries 2026-05-10 but its text is dated "May 11, 2026" and the pack index lists filing date 2026-05-11. The file-name date is not used as an authority. The purchase agreement for the preferred is dated May 10, 2026 (10-Q Q3 2026 page:74). - Extraction fidelity. Extraction is visible text only; no charts, images or speaker notes exist in these sources, and no presentation is supplied. Tables are flattened into lines, so column alignment must be checked against the page before a figure is read. At least one value is dropped in extraction: "is outstanding as of ) and (iv)" in the fee table footnote leaves a blank date (10-Q Q3 2026 page:167). A successful extraction is not a fidelity review; the figures sampled above matched across filing and release, but the schedule of investments pages (tens of pages in each 10-Q, for example roughly pages 5 to 66 of the Q3 10-Q extraction) were not read line by line in CP-0. - No filing conflicts found in the sampled facts. The Q3 10-Q liquidity text ("$111 in cash, cash equivalents, including money market funds, and foreign currency" and "$3,197 in borrowings available", page:141) agrees with the Q3 release and with Note 9.

- **Interest rate bases differ.** The Q3 release quotes a "weighted average stated interest rate on borrowings was 5.57%" (release page:3) and the Q2 release a "weighted average effective interest rate (including the effect of non-usage fees) was 5.49%" (EX-99.1 Q2 2026 page:3); the Q3 10-Q gives 5.72% for the nine months including non-usage fees (page:113). These are different bases and periods, not a conflict in the filing.

- **Date labels.** The Q1 release file name carries 2026-05-10 but its text is dated "May 11, 2026" and the pack index lists filing date 2026-05-11. The file-name date is not used as an authority. The purchase agreement for the preferred is dated May 10, 2026 (10-Q Q3 2026 page:74).

- **Extraction fidelity.** Extraction is visible text only; no charts, images or speaker notes exist in these sources, and no presentation is supplied. Tables are flattened into lines, so column alignment must be checked against the page before a figure is read. At least one value is dropped in extraction: "is outstanding as of ) and (iv)" in the fee table footnote leaves a blank date (10-Q Q3 2026 page:167). A successful extraction is not a fidelity review; the figures sampled above matched across filing and release, but the schedule of investments pages (tens of pages in each 10-Q, for example roughly pages 5 to 66 of the Q3 10-Q extraction) were not read line by line in CP-0.

- **No filing conflicts found in the sampled facts.** The Q3 10-Q liquidity text ("$111 in cash, cash equivalents, including money market funds, and foreign currency" and "$3,197 in borrowings available", page:141) agrees with the Q3 release and with Note 9.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is usable for a credit snapshot, with the issuer-specific metric set stated plainly. FS KKR Capital Corp is a business development company whose statements report investment income, net investment income, net assets and a statutory asset coverage test rather than EBITDA, so the leverage and interest cover chart fields are Not supplied and are replaced by debt to common equity, asset coverage and a net investment income based cover proxy, all labelled as calculations. Over nine months 2026 total investment income fell to 888 from 1,171, net assets fell by 850 to 4,999 as unrealised and realised losses of 766 and distributions of 375 outran net investment income of 366, and debt principal fell to 6,337 from 7,620 through asset sales and repayments. Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 111 of cash and foreign currency plus 3,197 of borrowings available, subject to borrowing base and other limits. The largest near-term claims are 900 of unsecured notes maturing in January and July 2027, and the main covenant is the revolver's minimum shareholders' equity floor of 3,750.0 after the May 8, 2026 amendment. Limits that matter: the credit agreement's definitions are not supplied, the borrowing base is not printed, and the cash and debt figures appear on several bases that this handoff labels one by one.

facts.label: Corrections to the CP-0 handoff
facts.text: - Covenant levels are partly printed. CP-0 said numeric financial covenant thresholds other than the 150% asset coverage test are not printed and that "minimum stockholders’ equity" has no level. The sources do print the revolver floor: Amendment No. 1 of May 8, 2026 provides for "a reset of the minimum Shareholders’ Equity floor to $3,750.0 from approximately $5,048.6" and a reduction of total commitments "to approximately $4,051.7 from $4,700.0" (10-Q Q1 2026 page:107; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:108). The 10-K lists the two financial covenants of the revolver: a minimum shareholders' equity measured at each fiscal quarter end and "a 150% asset coverage ratio" (10-K page:273). Still not supplied: the credit agreement's definition of shareholders' equity, the compliance certificate figures, and covenant levels for the Callowhill facility, the CLO notes and the note indentures beyond the asset coverage covenant. - Cash basis refinement. CP-0 said restricted cash was included in earlier net debt and excluded in the latest. The labels did change, but restricted cash was nil at June 30, 2026 (the Q2 cash flow footnote lists only cash of 107 and foreign currency of 2, 10-Q Q2 2026 page:5), so the Q2 and Q3 net debt cash figures (109 and 111) are on the same effective basis. The difference is that 4 of restricted cash sat inside the Q1 figure of 133 (10-Q Q1 2026 page:5) and 61 of restricted cash is outside the Q3 figure of 111 (10-Q Q3 2026 page:2). - Guarantors. CP-0 said no guarantor is named. The 10-K states that the revolver obligations "are guaranteed by certain of the Company’s subsidiaries" and secured "by a first priority security interest in substantially all of the assets of the Company and certain of the Company’s subsidiaries" (10-K page:273); the guarantors are not named.

facts.text: - Debt bases. Carrying value 6,231, principal 6,337 and 6,487 including preferred are three bases for the same capital; hedge accounting adjustments reduce the carrying value of four notes (10-Q Q3 page:110, footnote 7). Note 9 narrative says "As of December 31, 2025, $21 of such letters of credit have been issued" (10-K page:271) while the Note 9 table footnote says 50 (10-K pages 146, 261 and 282; repeated in 10-Q Q3 page:112). Availability of 3,117 plus outstanding 1,533 against commitments of 4,700 is consistent with 50, so 50 is used; the 21 matches the 2024 figure and looks stale. - Interest rate bases. 5.57% stated (Q3 release page:3), 5.49% effective at 2026-06-30 (10-Q Q2 page:107), 5.72% average for nine months (10-Q Q3 page:113) are different measures. - Realised proceeds. facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The business is a closed-end, externally managed business development company that lends mainly to private U.S. middle-market companies and is run by an adviser jointly operated by KKR Credit and an affiliate of Future Standard. Its creditors therefore face an asset manager's fee-and-distribution model rather than an operating company: income is investment income, the adviser is paid on gross assets and on income above a hurdle, and equity holders expect a quarterly distribution that the regulated investment company rules also require in substance. The 2026 transaction set is a package announced on May 11, 2026: a convertible preferred issue of 150 to a KKR affiliate, a tender offer by a KKR subsidiary, a 300 repurchase authorization and a 50% incentive fee waiver for four quarters, alongside a revolver amendment dated May 8, 2026, an issue of 900 of 7.500% unsecured notes on June 8, 2026 and the termination of two secured facilities on June 29, 2026. The documented behaviour is mixed rather than adverse: sponsor capital and a fee waiver are supportive, share repurchases and special distributions draw on the same cash that could reduce debt, and no priming, collateral release or non-pro-rata exchange appears in the sources. Five stockholder suits filed from May 4, 2026 allege misstatements about valuations, restructuring and the distribution strategy, which links governance to the quality of reported net asset value that supports the asset coverage and equity floor tests. The main limits are that ownership of common stock, the executed purchase and advisory agreements and the use of proceeds of the new notes are not in the pack.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: On May 11, 2026 the Company announced, with its first quarter results, four actions it called strategic value enhancement actions: a 150 cumulative convertible perpetual preferred investment by a KKR subsidiary, a fixed price tender offer by a KKR subsidiary for up to 150 of common stock at 11.00 per share, a 300 share repurchase program, and a waiver of 50% of the subordinated income incentive fee for four consecutive quarters (Q1 release pages 2 and 3). The preferred closed on June 29, 2026 with 6,000,000 shares sold at 25.00 to KKR Alternative Assets L.P. under a purchase agreement dated May 10, 2026 (10-Q Q3 2026 page:74), paying 5.00% in cash or, at the Company's option, 7.00% in kind, rising by 1.00% a year after 5.5 years, with a conversion price of 18.83, the March 31, 2026 net asset value per share. It ranks senior to common stock and, per the release, "junior to all existing indebtedness"; the Company may redeem it in cash at any time with board approval, holders may convert after six months and may require cash redemption at par after six years on 90 days' notice, and a majority of holders can require redemption on a change of control (10-Q Q3 2026 pages 81 to 83). The Company states it will use the proceeds for general corporate purposes including repurchases or debt repayment (10-Q Q2 2026 page:158). The Q2 release says the tender offer "was successfully completed", the preferred closed and the repurchase program commenced (Q2 release page:2); the number of shares KKR acquired in the tender and its resulting ownership are not supplied. Status of the package at 2026-09-30 is therefore closed for the preferred and tender, ongoing for the repurchase program (6,533,672 shares for 73 through September 30, plus 1,546,162 shares for 17 in October) and running for the fee waiver, which has no recoupment (10-Q Q3 2026 pages 75, 77 and 123).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: New and changed debt in the period are as follows. The Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility was amended on May 8, 2026 (Amendment No. 1, reported as a Q1 subsequent event) to cut total commitments to about 4,051.7 from 4,700.0, to raise the applicable margins for extending lenders by 0.125 percentage points in each pricing tier, and to reset the minimum shareholders' equity floor to 3,750.0 from about 5,048.6 (10-Q Q1 2026 page:107; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:108). On June 8, 2026 the Company issued 900 of 7.500% Notes due August 1, 2031 under a Sixteenth Supplemental Indenture to the 2014 base indenture, with the trustee U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association; the notes are general unsecured obligations that "rank effectively junior to any of the Company’s secured indebtedness" and are structurally junior to subsidiary debt, carry covenants requiring compliance with the statutory asset coverage requirement, and give holders a change of control repurchase offer at 100% of principal (10-Q Q2 2026 pages 108 and 109). A swap of 900 notional to floating was entered at issuance (10-Q Q2 2026 page:95). The coupon is well above the 3.400% of the notes that reached their listed maturity of January 15, 2026; the use of proceeds of the new notes is not stated in the sources read, though the Q2 filing shows lower revolver borrowings in the same quarter. On June 29, 2026 the Meadowbrook Run and CCT Tokyo Funding secured facilities were terminated with realised losses of 2 and 0 respectively (10-Q Q2 2026 page:109). Earlier new debt that remains outstanding is the Callowhill facility (June 2, 2025, up to 400), the CLO-2 financing of 380 (March 28, 2025) and the CLO-3 financing of 389.5 closed December 18, 2025 (10-K pages 266, 277 and 278). Subsequent to the quarter and before the as-of date, the board on October 7, 2026 declared a regular distribution of 0.44 and a special distribution of 0.20 per share, and on October 28, 2026 a preferred dividend of 0.3125 per share (10-Q Q3 2026 page:123); the special distribution is described as a portion of estimated accumulated spillback income (Q3 release page:2). No further debt issue, amendment or refinancing after September 30, 2026 appears in the sources up to the cutoff.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: FS KKR Capital Corp's creditors are adequately protected in the near term, but the credit is weakening because the equity value beneath the debt is shrinking. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 3,308 million against USD 900 million of notes maturing in 2027, asset coverage of 179% on debt against the 150% minimum, and a lender-agreed lower equity floor of USD 3,750.0 million. The weakest point is the fall in net asset value per share from USD 20.89 to USD 18.28 over nine months 2026, with investment income down 24.2% as the portfolio shrinks, distributions above net investment income and five stockholder suits with no loss estimate. What decides the outcome is whether portfolio marks stabilise and non-accruals, at 3.4% of fair value, keep falling, because the covenants and the asset coverage test all run off net asset value. [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 figures; CP-1A governance and litigation rows]

[Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 figures; CP-1A governance and litigation rows]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The equity cushion under the debt is eroding even as debt falls. Over nine months 2026 common equity fell by USD 850 million to USD 4,999 million, net asset value per share fell from USD 20.89 to USD 18.28, and realised and unrealised losses of USD 766 million outran net investment income of USD 366 million, while debt principal fell 16.8% to USD 6,337 million. Because the debt reduction came from asset sales and repayments rather than retained earnings, debt principal to common equity eased only from 130.3% to 126.8%, so creditors still depend on portfolio marks to hold the cushion. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics and Calculations]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is adequate for the next two years but the later wall is larger. The issuer holds USD 111 million of cash and USD 3,197 million of availability, subject to a borrowing base that is not printed, which is 3.68 times the USD 900 million of notes due in January and July 2027 and 2.14 times unfunded commitments of USD 1,545.4 million. No committed facility expires within twelve months. Maturities then rise to USD 1,000 million in 2029, USD 1,644 million in 2030 and USD 1,300 million in 2031, USD 3,944 million in total or 62.2% of principal debt, and the 7.500% coupon on the USD 900 million of 2031 notes issued on June 8, 2026 compares with 3.400% on the notes that reached maturity in January 2026, so refinancing will cost more. [Documentary Fact for the schedule; Analyst Interpretation for the wall; CP-1 debt maturities; CP-1A transaction summary]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The nearest covenant constraint is the equity floor, not the leverage ratio. On May 8, 2026 lenders agreed to cut revolver commitments to about USD 4,051.7 million from USD 4,700.0 million, raise margins and reset the minimum shareholders' equity floor to USD 3,750.0 million from about USD 5,048.6 million. Common equity of USD 4,999 million is USD 1,249.0 million, or 25.0%, above the new floor on a proxy basis, which equals a fall of about 11.0% in investment fair value; asset coverage would take roughly a 15% to 16% fall in its base to reach 150%. Equity at 2026-09-30 was USD 49.6 million below the former floor, so, on this proxy, the amendment avoided a breach. The credit agreement's definition of equity is not supplied, so this ordering is an interpretation. [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Covenants and headroom]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings no longer cover the shareholder distribution without sponsor support. Investment income fell 21.2% in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 and net investment income was USD 127 million, after a USD 12 million incentive fee waiver that runs to the quarter ending March 31, 2027 with no recoupment. Net investment income covered 105.0% of Q3 common distributions of USD 121 million with the waiver and 95.0% without it, and 98.1% over nine months, while a special distribution of USD 0.20 per share and a regular USD 0.44 were declared for the fourth quarter. When the waiver ends, the same income would leave distributions about USD 12 million a quarter less covered, so either the distribution, the portfolio size or net asset value must give; each reduces the cushion or the cash available to reduce debt. [Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the consequence; CP-1 Earnings and income quality; CP-1A fee waiver row]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The debt structure puts the unsecured notes behind secured claims that can grow. The issuer has USD 4,650 million of unsecured notes against USD 1,687 million of secured debt, 73.4% and 26.6% of principal debt. The revolver is secured on substantially all assets of the Company and certain subsidiaries and has USD 3,134 million of availability, so secured borrowing ahead of the notes can rise subject to the borrowing base and the 150% asset coverage test; the 7.500% notes state they rank effectively junior to secured debt and are structurally junior to subsidiary debt. As a balance sheet mechanic and not a recovery estimate, investments at fair value less secured debt are 2.07 times the unsecured notes today. The joint venture, worth 32.7% of common equity, also carries USD 2,330.9 million of its own debt that ranks ahead of the issuer in its assets. [Documentary Fact for the structure; Analyst Interpretation for the mechanics; CP-1 Debt schedule; CP-1A Company and operating model]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Sponsor support is real but small against the decline, and governance carries open items. A KKR affiliate paid USD 150 million for convertible preferred stock that ranks junior to debt, a KKR subsidiary ran a tender offer, and the adviser waived half its subordinated income incentive fee, but the USD 150 million is 17.6% of the USD 850 million fall in equity and the preferred carries two board seats, a change-of-control put and a holder put after six years. Share repurchases of USD 90 million through October 30, 2026 use the same cash that could reduce debt. Five stockholder suits allege misleading statements on valuations and distributions, two challenge adviser fees, and the Company states it cannot estimate a loss. No priming, uptiering, collateral release or non-pro-rata exchange is documented, but the executed agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity for such steps is not assessed. [Documentary Fact for the actions; Analyst Interpretation for the weighting; CP-1A governance, ownership and conflicts rows]

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 3,308 million of cash plus availability, no committed facility expiring within twelve months and USD 900 million due in 2027, so near-term debt service and refinancing are covered unless the borrowing base falls sharply. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 liquidity and maturities]. Loan book quality and seniority: 63.2% senior secured across 234 portfolio companies, top ten exposure of 21%, a 10.0% yield on accruing debt and non-accruals down from 4.2% to 3.4% of fair value since March 31, 2026, which supports interest income and marks. [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model; CP-1 Financials]. Statutory and covenant headroom with lender support: asset coverage of 179% on debt against a 150% minimum, a lender-agreed lower equity floor and compliance reported at 2026-09-30, which show lenders willing to adjust terms rather than restrict the facility. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the lender reading; CP-1 Covenants]. Sponsor alignment: preferred capital, a tender, a four-quarter fee waiver with no recoupment and an adviser jointly run by KKR Credit and Future Standard give creditors an engaged sponsor, though the support is limited in size. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A governance rows]. Rate balance: a 100 basis point rise adds USD 27 million to twelve-month net interest income and a fall removes the same, with USD 2,600 million of fixed-rate notes swapped to floating, so rate moves do not threaten debt service on their own. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 debt schedule and earnings notes].

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filed sources support the downstream snapshot with limitations: statements, debt schedule, liquidity, leverage and 2026 capital actions are located, but covenant levels, ratings and underlying financing documents are absent. | Medium | No credit agreements, indentures, ratings or investor presentations were supplied; covenant thresholds beyond asset coverage cannot be read, and the cash definition changed between releases. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Filed statements and the full debt schedule are readable for the third quarter of 2026 and for FY2025. | Leverage, liquidity and maturity work can start from filed figures rather than management claims. | High |

| The issuer is a business development company, so corporate measures such as EBITDA and segment margins do not map. | Credit metrics must rest on investment income, net asset value, asset coverage and debt rather than industrial-style cash flow. | Medium |

| Covenant thresholds, ratings and the underlying financing agreements are not in the pack. | Headroom against lender tests cannot be measured beyond the disclosed asset coverage and a compliance statement. | High |

| The joint venture with an outside investor is described only through selected balance sheet and income data. | Its own debt and look-through exposure can be noted but not analysed in depth. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for all four selected consumers. The filed 10-K and three filed 10-Qs carry the statements, the note on financing arrangements, liquidity discussion, commitments, financial highlights and subsequent events for the issuer's own consolidated perimeter, and three earnings releases add attributed management narrative and the 2026 capital actions. Nothing blocks a consumer on identity, period or perimeter. The limitations are bounded: no executed financing documents, no ratings or market quotes, no investor presentations, and a business development company structure that changes which credit metrics exist. Readiness here is source sufficiency only; it does not say that any downstream analysis is complete or that any figure has been normalised or reconciled.
### Source-by-source assessment

- **Entity and perimeter.** The registrant is a single legal entity filing consolidated statements. Note 1 describes it as an "externally managed, non-diversified, closed-end management investment company" with "various wholly-owned subsidiaries, including special-purpose financing subsidiaries" (10-Q Q3 2026 page:67). The adviser is FS/KKR Advisor, LLC (10-K FY2025 page:4: "We are managed by FS/KKR Advisor, LLC"). Borrowings of the financing subsidiaries count as the Company's: "Borrowings of each of the Company’s wholly-owned, special-purpose financing subsidiaries are considered borrowings of the Company" (10-Q Q3 2026 page:113). No separate issuer, guarantor or restricted/unrestricted group is named in the sources read; the notes and credit-facility names (Callowhill, Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility, CLO-2, CLO-3) are borrowing vehicles inside the consolidated perimeter.

- **Original authority.** The 10-K and 10-Qs are filed statements and control their facts. The three earnings releases are management presentations of the same quarters and carry non-GAAP measures (adjusted net investment income, net debt); they are attributed supporting claims and cannot override the filings. Where the release and the 10-Q show the same item they agree on the points sampled (net asset value per share $18.28 and total assets $11,695 in both the Q3 release pages 8 and 9 and the Q3 10-Q pages 2 and 3).

- **Periods and basis.** Current period Q3 2026 is covered by the Q3 10-Q (three and nine months ended September 30, 2026) and the Q3 release. The prior period FY2025 is covered by the 10-K and by the December 31, 2025 comparative column in each 2026 10-Q (for example 10-Q Q3 2026 page:2, "Total assets $ 11,695 $ 13,729"). The Q1 and Q2 10-Qs and releases provide the intermediate quarters for a discrete Q1, Q2, Q3 view; the Q2 10-Q gives six-month and the Q3 10-Q nine-month cumulative columns, so quarter versus year-to-date must stay labelled. All amounts are USD millions unless marked; the senior revolver also holds euro, sterling and Australian dollar borrowings translated to USD (10-Q Q3 2026 page:110, footnote 4).

- **Version relationships.** Each filing is the original for its period. No amendments (10-K/A, 10-Q/A) are in the pack. The pack does not hold any executed indenture, credit agreement, purchase agreement or supplement, so no base-versus-amendment question arises.

- **Debt and liquidity evidence located.** Note 9 lists every financing arrangement with rate, amount outstanding, amount available and maturity, and gives the total: "Total $ 6,487 $ 3,197" including the $150 convertible preferred (10-Q Q3 2026 page:110). The senior revolver availability is stated net of standby letters of credit: "As of September 30, 2026, $50 of such letters of credit have been issued" (page:110). A December 31, 2025 table is on page:111. The 10-K carries the full note (10-K FY2025 page:259 onward, with the indenture descriptions on pages 274 to 276). Liquidity text, unfunded commitments and the asset coverage discussion are on 10-Q Q3 2026 pages 141 to 143; the 10-K equivalent is on page:144.

- **Covenant evidence located.** The only compliance statement is generic: "The Company was in compliance with all covenants required by its financing arrangements as of September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025" (10-Q Q3 2026 page:113). The 10-K says the covenants "require us and our subsidiaries to, among other things, maintain certain financial ratios, including asset coverage and minimum stockholders’ equity" (10-K FY2025 page:93) without printing a threshold. The statutory asset coverage test is quantified in the 10-Q: coverage on senior securities representing indebtedness of 179% and on senior securities that are stock of 177%, against a 150% requirement (page:109 and pages 142 to 143).

- **Subsequent events and the cutoff.** All seven sources were filed on or before 2026-11-05, so nothing postdates the cutoff. The Q3 10-Q and Q3 release were filed on the as-of date itself. Subsequent events are in the 10-Q Q3 2026 Note 13 (page:123) and release page:2: repurchases from October 1 through October 30, 2026, a declared fourth quarter distribution, a declared special distribution and a declared preferred dividend. Future payment dates in those items are declared terms, not events after the cutoff.

- **Transaction and ownership evidence.** The 2026 capital actions are documented: the May release announces a $150 million convertible preferred from a KKR subsidiary, a $150 million tender offer, a $300 million repurchase program and a 50% incentive fee waiver (EX-99.1 Q1 2026 pages 2 and 3); the Q3 10-Q share transactions note records the preferred issue on June 29, 2026 to KKR Alternative Assets L.P. (page:74) and the $900 principal 7.500% Notes due 2031 issued June 8, 2026 appear in the Q2 10-Q (page:95) and the Q3 note table. Governing documents (purchase agreement, advisory agreement) are referenced but not supplied.

- **Joint venture.** Credit Opportunities Partners JV, LLC is a 50/50 voting joint venture with South Carolina Retirement Systems Group Trust; the 10-Q gives selected balance sheet and income data (10-Q Q3 2026 page:94), including the joint venture's own debt, which is not the issuer's borrowing. The venture's full statements are not supplied.
### Conflicts, definitional differences and extraction cautions

- **Cash basis changed.** The Q2 release nets "Cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash and foreign currency $ (109 )" in net debt (EX-99.1 Q2 2026 page:10), with restricted cash defined as "cash collateral required to be posted pursuant to the Company’s derivative contracts" (page:12). The Q3 release nets "Cash, cash equivalents, and foreign currency ($111)" (EX-99.1 Q3 2026 page:9), while the Q3 balance sheet shows "Restricted cash 61" separately (10-Q Q3 2026 page:2). The Q3 cash flow statement ends at "$ 172" including "restricted cash of $61" (page:5). The reported net debt-to-equity ratios (122% for Q2, 125% for Q3) are therefore not on an identical cash basis. Downstream modules must label which cash they use; CP-0 does not restate.

- **Three debt figures.** The Q3 balance sheet shows "Debt (net of deferred financing costs and discount of $46 and $45, respectively) 6,231" (10-Q page:2), the Q3 release shows "Debt outstanding (principal) $6,337" (release page:9), and Note 9 totals "$ 6,487" including the convertible preferred (page:110). Footnote 7 on page:110 identifies hedge-accounting carrying adjustments on four notes. The differences are of basis (carrying versus principal versus including preferred); CP-0 does not reconcile them, and CP-1 must carry the basis with each figure.

- **Interest rate bases differ.** The Q3 release quotes a "weighted average stated interest rate on borrowings was 5.57%" (release page:3) and the Q2 release a "weighted average effective interest rate (including the effect of non-usage fees) was 5.49%" (EX-99.1 Q2 2026 page:3); the Q3 10-Q gives 5.72% for the nine months including non-usage fees (page:113). These are different bases and periods, not a conflict in the filing.

- **Date labels.** The Q1 release file name carries 2026-05-10 but its text is dated "May 11, 2026" and the pack index lists filing date 2026-05-11. The file-name date is not used as an authority. The purchase agreement for the preferred is dated May 10, 2026 (10-Q Q3 2026 page:74).

- **Extraction fidelity.** Extraction is visible text only; no charts, images or speaker notes exist in these sources, and no presentation is supplied. Tables are flattened into lines, so column alignment must be checked against the page before a figure is read. At least one value is dropped in extraction: "is outstanding as of ) and (iv)" in the fee table footnote leaves a blank date (10-Q Q3 2026 page:167). A successful extraction is not a fidelity review; the figures sampled above matched across filing and release, but the schedule of investments pages (tens of pages in each 10-Q, for example roughly pages 5 to 66 of the Q3 10-Q extraction) were not read line by line in CP-0.

- **No filing conflicts found in the sampled facts.** The Q3 10-Q liquidity text ("$111 in cash, cash equivalents, including money market funds, and foreign currency" and "$3,197 in borrowings available", page:141) agrees with the Q3 release and with Note 9.
### Consumer assessment
| Consumer | Readiness | Evidence located | Limitations carried forward |

| CP-1 canonical data foundation | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Statements of operations, balance sheets, cash flows, net assets, Note 9 debt tables, financial highlights, asset coverage and non-GAAP reconciliations for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 and FY2025 | Business development company: no EBITDA, capex or segments (single segment, 10-Q Q3 2026 page:123); covenant levels unprinted; cash basis and debt basis differ across sources; quarter versus year-to-date must stay labelled |

| CP-1A business and transaction context | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description in the 10-K (page:4), adviser relationship, KKR-related 2026 capital actions, share repurchase, joint venture, subsequent events | Context carries no deal terms, sector, sponsor or parent; executed purchase and advisory agreements not supplied; ownership beyond filing disclosure not supplied |

| CP-2 fundamental credit synthesis | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Depends on CP-1 and CP-1A registers; source set gives credit-relevant drivers (non-accrual share, net asset value trend, leverage, liquidity, maturities) | No ratings, market quotes, peers or covenant thresholds; synthesis inherits every CP-1 and CP-1A limitation |

| CP-5 evidence trace validator | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Seven pinned sources with page locators allow quote and figure checks against filings | Management-release claims need filing support; presentations absent, so no slide-level trace exists |
## Calculations
No analytical calculation was performed or needed in CP-0. Only coverage counts were tallied from the extraction headers.
| Item | Inputs | Result |
| Filing pages in the four filed periodic reports | 298 (10-K) + 157 (Q1 10-Q) + 169 (Q2 10-Q) + 169 (Q3 10-Q) | 793 |
| Release pages in the three earnings releases | 12 (Q1) + 12 (Q2) + 11 (Q3) | 35 |
| Total extraction pages across the seven sources | 793 + 35 | 828 |

Coverage statement: all 828 extraction pages are retained as evidence. Pages read in CP-0 were targeted to the statements, financing notes, liquidity, subsequent events, covenant and rating terms, and the three releases in full; the remaining pages (mainly the schedules of investments, fair value tables, risk factors and tax notes) are retained but not individually reviewed here and carry no CP-0 claim.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| Credit agreements, indentures, CLO documents and the convertible preferred terms are not supplied; only the notes summarise them (10-Q Q3 2026 pages 109 to 111) | Medium | CP-1, CP-2, CP-5 | Obtain executed facility and indenture documents if covenant-level analysis is required; otherwise report covenant headroom as Not supplied |

| Numeric financial covenant thresholds other than the statutory 150% asset coverage are not printed; "minimum stockholders’ equity" has no level (10-K FY2025 page:93) | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | State Not supplied; use disclosed asset coverage of 179% and 177% and the compliance statement only |

| No rating of the issuer or its notes was found when the sources were searched for rating terms, and there are no market quotes or peers (context fields are empty; the filings discuss ratings only for portfolio investments, generically, and as a risk factor) | Medium | CP-2 | Treat ratings and relative value as Not supplied; do not infer from filings |
| No investor presentations; 3 of 3 quarters have a release only | Low | CP-1A, CP-5 | Use releases as attributed management claims; no slide-level coverage can be claimed |

| Cash definition differs between the Q2 and Q3 releases, and debt appears on three bases | Medium | CP-1, CP-2, CP-5 | Label basis on every figure; do not mix net debt ratios across quarters without restating cash |

| Business development company structure: no EBITDA, segment, capex or cash-conversion data in the usual form | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Use investment income, net investment income, net asset value, non-accrual share and asset coverage as the metric set; say so explicitly |

| Joint venture and affiliated portfolio companies appear only as selected data | Low | CP-1A, CP-2 | Note the venture's own debt as outside the issuer's borrowings; Not supplied for its full statements |

| Context holds no deal terms, sector, sponsor, parent or guarantors; governing agreements for the KKR capital actions not supplied | Low | CP-1A | Rely on filing and release disclosure; leave unfilled fields as Not supplied |

| Text extraction only: tables flattened, one dropped date in the fee table (10-Q Q3 2026 page:167); schedules of investments not reviewed line by line | Low | CP-1, CP-5 | Check column alignment on the page before reading any figure; re-open the source page for every quote |
## Next module
CP-1 (canonical data foundation) can run now on the pinned sources. Instructions for it:
- Use the Q3 10-Q (Q3 2026 and nine months), the Q1 and Q2 10-Qs for discrete quarters and the 10-K for FY2025; keep the Q3 release only for attributed non-GAAP measures.

- Build the debt table from Note 9 (10-Q Q3 2026 pages 109 to 111, 10-K FY2025 page:259 onward), label carrying value, principal and total including preferred, and keep the letters of credit deduction from availability.
- Put cash on one stated basis and show the restricted cash of $61 separately; do not compare the 122% and 125% net debt ratios without saying the bases differ.
- Carry forward: business development company metric set, no covenant thresholds, no ratings, single segment, and quarter versus year-to-date labels.
CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 follow in dependency order and inherit every limitation in the Gaps section.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Leverage eased slightly as the portfolio shrank and net assets eroded: principal debt is 6,337 against common equity of 4,999, with asset coverage of 179% on debt versus a 150% minimum and 3,197 of availability. | Medium | No EBITDA exists; covenant definitions and borrowing base values are not supplied, so headroom rests on the reported equity figure and asset coverage ratios only. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Net asset value per share fell from 20.89 to 18.28 over nine months 2026 while debt principal fell from 7,620 to 6,337. | Deleveraging came from asset sales and repayments, not earnings growth; the equity cushion under the debt is thinner. | High |

| The main bank covenant is a minimum shareholders' equity floor, reset on May 8, 2026 to 3,750.0 from about 5,048.6. | Common equity of 4,999 clears the new floor by about 1,249 but is below the old floor, so the reset mattered. | Medium |

| Nine-month net investment income of 366 did not cover common distributions of 373, and the Q3 figure relied on a 12 fee waiver. | Distribution policy competes with debt reduction for cash; the waiver is temporary. | Medium |

| Liquidity of 3,308 (cash 111 plus availability 3,197) compares with 900 of notes maturing in 2027 and unfunded commitments of 1,545.4. | Near-term refinancing looks covered if the borrowing base holds; availability is secured and base-limited. | Medium |

| Unsecured notes of 4,650 sit alongside 1,687 of secured borrowings; five stockholder suits filed since May 2026 carry no loss estimate. | Unsecured creditors rank behind secured lenders (the 7.500% notes say so); the suits are an unquantified contingent claim alleging misstatements on valuations. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The financial base is usable for a credit snapshot, with the issuer-specific metric set stated plainly. FS KKR Capital Corp is a business development company whose statements report investment income, net investment income, net assets and a statutory asset coverage test rather than EBITDA, so the leverage and interest cover chart fields are Not supplied and are replaced by debt to common equity, asset coverage and a net investment income based cover proxy, all labelled as calculations. Over nine months 2026 total investment income fell to 888 from 1,171, net assets fell by 850 to 4,999 as unrealised and realised losses of 766 and distributions of 375 outran net investment income of 366, and debt principal fell to 6,337 from 7,620 through asset sales and repayments. Liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 111 of cash and foreign currency plus 3,197 of borrowings available, subject to borrowing base and other limits. The largest near-term claims are 900 of unsecured notes maturing in January and July 2027, and the main covenant is the revolver's minimum shareholders' equity floor of 3,750.0 after the May 8, 2026 amendment. Limits that matter: the credit agreement's definitions are not supplied, the borrowing base is not printed, and the cash and debt figures appear on several bases that this handoff labels one by one.
### Corrections to the CP-0 handoff
The earlier handoff cannot be edited, so the corrections are stated here and govern downstream use.

- **Covenant levels are partly printed.** CP-0 said numeric financial covenant thresholds other than the 150% asset coverage test are not printed and that "minimum stockholders’ equity" has no level. The sources do print the revolver floor: Amendment No. 1 of May 8, 2026 provides for "a reset of the minimum Shareholders’ Equity floor to $3,750.0 from approximately $5,048.6" and a reduction of total commitments "to approximately $4,051.7 from $4,700.0" (10-Q Q1 2026 page:107; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:108). The 10-K lists the two financial covenants of the revolver: a minimum shareholders' equity measured at each fiscal quarter end and "a 150% asset coverage ratio" (10-K page:273). Still not supplied: the credit agreement's definition of shareholders' equity, the compliance certificate figures, and covenant levels for the Callowhill facility, the CLO notes and the note indentures beyond the asset coverage covenant.

- **Cash basis refinement.** CP-0 said restricted cash was included in earlier net debt and excluded in the latest. The labels did change, but restricted cash was nil at June 30, 2026 (the Q2 cash flow footnote lists only cash of 107 and foreign currency of 2, 10-Q Q2 2026 page:5), so the Q2 and Q3 net debt cash figures (109 and 111) are on the same effective basis. The difference is that 4 of restricted cash sat inside the Q1 figure of 133 (10-Q Q1 2026 page:5) and 61 of restricted cash is outside the Q3 figure of 111 (10-Q Q3 2026 page:2).

- **Guarantors.** CP-0 said no guarantor is named. The 10-K states that the revolver obligations "are guaranteed by certain of the Company’s subsidiaries" and secured "by a first priority security interest in substantially all of the assets of the Company and certain of the Company’s subsidiaries" (10-K page:273); the guarantors are not named.
### Chart data: leverage

### Definition review and conflicts

- **Debt bases.** Carrying value 6,231, principal 6,337 and 6,487 including preferred are three bases for the same capital; hedge accounting adjustments reduce the carrying value of four notes (10-Q Q3 page:110, footnote 7). Always label the basis.

- **Net debt.** The release's net debt of 6,271 is principal debt plus preferred, less cash and foreign currency of 111 and net receivable for investments sold of 105 (Q3 release page:9). It excludes 61 of restricted cash; with it included the ratio would be lower (calculated 124%).

- **Cash basis by quarter.** Q1 management cash of 133 included 4 restricted; Q2 109 had none; Q3 111 excludes 61. This handoff's liquidity chart uses one basis (excluding restricted cash) in all four periods.

- **Letters of credit conflict in the 10-K.** Note 9 narrative says "As of December 31, 2025, $21 of such letters of credit have been issued" (10-K page:271) while the Note 9 table footnote says 50 (10-K pages 146, 261 and 282; repeated in 10-Q Q3 page:112). Availability of 3,117 plus outstanding 1,533 against commitments of 4,700 is consistent with 50, so 50 is used; the 21 matches the 2024 figure and looks stale.
- **Interest rate bases.** 5.57% stated (Q3 release page:3), 5.49% effective at 2026-06-30 (10-Q Q2 page:107), 5.72% average for nine months (10-Q Q3 page:113) are different measures.
- **Realised proceeds.** The cash flow proceeds of 646 for Q3 differ from the release's 442 of sales and repayments because the receivable for investments sold fell from 310 to 106; see Calculations.

### Business and transaction view

The business is a closed-end, externally managed business development company that lends mainly to private U.S. middle-market companies and is run by an adviser jointly operated by KKR Credit and an affiliate of Future Standard. Its creditors therefore face an asset manager's fee-and-distribution model rather than an operating company: income is investment income, the adviser is paid on gross assets and on income above a hurdle, and equity holders expect a quarterly distribution that the regulated investment company rules also require in substance. The 2026 transaction set is a package announced on May 11, 2026: a convertible preferred issue of 150 to a KKR affiliate, a tender offer by a KKR subsidiary, a 300 repurchase authorization and a 50% incentive fee waiver for four quarters, alongside a revolver amendment dated May 8, 2026, an issue of 900 of 7.500% unsecured notes on June 8, 2026 and the termination of two secured facilities on June 29, 2026. The documented behaviour is mixed rather than adverse: sponsor capital and a fee waiver are supportive, share repurchases and special distributions draw on the same cash that could reduce debt, and no priming, collateral release or non-pro-rata exchange appears in the sources. Five stockholder suits filed from May 4, 2026 allege misstatements about valuations, restructuring and the distribution strategy, which links governance to the quality of reported net asset value that supports the asset coverage and equity floor tests. The main limits are that ownership of common stock, the executed purchase and advisory agreements and the use of proceeds of the new notes are not in the pack.
### Corrections to earlier handoffs
These corrections govern downstream use; the earlier handoffs cannot be edited.

- **CP-1 on the joint venture.** The CP-1 income quality note says affiliated and controlled dividend and other income of 84 in Q3 2026 came from affiliated and controlled investments "including the joint venture". The 10-Q Q3 2026 statements (page:3) show only that the 84 is the sum of 28 (non-controlled affiliated) and 56 (controlled affiliated) with nil from unaffiliated investments; they do not say how much, if any, came from the joint venture. Treat the joint venture share as not supplied.

- **CP-1 on the CCT Tokyo facility.** CP-1 listed the CCT Tokyo Funding facility as gone at its listed maturity of June 2, 2026. The 10-Q Q2 2026 (page:109) states that on June 29, 2026 "Tokyo Funding terminated the committed facility arrangement with SMBC". Both it and Meadowbrook Run were terminated on June 29, 2026.

- **CP-1 on Q1 leverage.** The CP-1 Q1 2026 leverage chart row says "the release prints debt to equity of 138% and net debt to equity of 131%". The 138% is printed in the Q2 release (EX-99.1 Q2 2026 page:1); the Q1 release prints only the net ratio of 131% (EX-99.1 Q1 2026 page:1). The CP-1 financial table cites this correctly.
- **CP-0 on covenant levels** was already corrected in CP-1 and stays corrected: the revolver equity floor is 3,750.0.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On May 11, 2026 the Company announced, with its first quarter results, four actions it called strategic value enhancement actions: a 150 cumulative convertible perpetual preferred investment by a KKR subsidiary, a fixed price tender offer by a KKR subsidiary for up to 150 of common stock at 11.00 per share, a 300 share repurchase program, and a waiver of 50% of the subordinated income incentive fee for four consecutive quarters (Q1 release pages 2 and 3). The preferred closed on June 29, 2026 with 6,000,000 shares sold at 25.00 to KKR Alternative Assets L.P. under a purchase agreement dated May 10, 2026 (10-Q Q3 2026 page:74), paying 5.00% in cash or, at the Company's option, 7.00% in kind, rising by 1.00% a year after 5.5 years, with a conversion price of 18.83, the March 31, 2026 net asset value per share. It ranks senior to common stock and, per the release, "junior to all existing indebtedness"; the Company may redeem it in cash at any time with board approval, holders may convert after six months and may require cash redemption at par after six years on 90 days' notice, and a majority of holders can require redemption on a change of control (10-Q Q3 2026 pages 81 to 83). The Company states it will use the proceeds for general corporate purposes including repurchases or debt repayment (10-Q Q2 2026 page:158). The Q2 release says the tender offer "was successfully completed", the preferred closed and the repurchase program commenced (Q2 release page:2); the number of shares KKR acquired in the tender and its resulting ownership are not supplied. Status of the package at 2026-09-30 is therefore closed for the preferred and tender, ongoing for the repurchase program (6,533,672 shares for 73 through September 30, plus 1,546,162 shares for 17 in October) and running for the fee waiver, which has no recoupment (10-Q Q3 2026 pages 75, 77 and 123).

New and changed debt in the period are as follows. The Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility was amended on May 8, 2026 (Amendment No. 1, reported as a Q1 subsequent event) to cut total commitments to about 4,051.7 from 4,700.0, to raise the applicable margins for extending lenders by 0.125 percentage points in each pricing tier, and to reset the minimum shareholders' equity floor to 3,750.0 from about 5,048.6 (10-Q Q1 2026 page:107; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:108). On June 8, 2026 the Company issued 900 of 7.500% Notes due August 1, 2031 under a Sixteenth Supplemental Indenture to the 2014 base indenture, with the trustee U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association; the notes are general unsecured obligations that "rank effectively junior to any of the Company’s secured indebtedness" and are structurally junior to subsidiary debt, carry covenants requiring compliance with the statutory asset coverage requirement, and give holders a change of control repurchase offer at 100% of principal (10-Q Q2 2026 pages 108 and 109). A swap of 900 notional to floating was entered at issuance (10-Q Q2 2026 page:95). The coupon is well above the 3.400% of the notes that reached their listed maturity of January 15, 2026; the use of proceeds of the new notes is not stated in the sources read, though the Q2 filing shows lower revolver borrowings in the same quarter. On June 29, 2026 the Meadowbrook Run and CCT Tokyo Funding secured facilities were terminated with realised losses of 2 and 0 respectively (10-Q Q2 2026 page:109). Earlier new debt that remains outstanding is the Callowhill facility (June 2, 2025, up to 400), the CLO-2 financing of 380 (March 28, 2025) and the CLO-3 financing of 389.5 closed December 18, 2025 (10-K pages 266, 277 and 278). Subsequent to the quarter and before the as-of date, the board on October 7, 2026 declared a regular distribution of 0.44 and a special distribution of 0.20 per share, and on October 28, 2026 a preferred dividend of 0.3125 per share (10-Q Q3 2026 page:123); the special distribution is described as a portion of estimated accumulated spillback income (Q3 release page:2). No further debt issue, amendment or refinancing after September 30, 2026 appears in the sources up to the cutoff.

spans.text: ## Request

Module CP-2 (fundamental credit synthesis) for FS KKR Capital Corp (NYSE: FSK), credit_snapshot pathway, as of 2026-11-05 (cutoff 2026-11-05). It synthesises the upstream financial base and the business and transaction context into a creditor's fundamental credit view, in USD, for Q3 2026 against FY2025. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources
### Issuer sources

This module works from upstream handoffs only and quotes no source text. The pinned sources below stand behind those handoffs; figures used here were spot-checked against them (Note 9 totals, balance sheet, income statement, Q3 liquidity discussion, covenant amendment text) and are cited to the handoffs, not to source pages.
| Source (exact name) | sha256 (pinned file) |
Run settings (dates, currency and scope only): context sha256 378a6255aee6dac53a389f9bf4cbce2419e6f8121d5d4932c50d57d1600eb13a.
### Supplied handoffs
| Module | sha256 | Role here |
| CP-0 | 6fa09daba39205fb415654f095188714149fb623a5ac6f52a41f3d1dba8bb321 | Source readiness and limits; READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for CP-2 |
| CP-1 | 3041d0a971deb9687f6b6c966a852ccaab08ba47aa98c5992b8b989d073887d8 | Financial base: statements, debt schedule, liquidity, covenants, calculated metrics |
| CP-1A | 43fb1cbbafd205e1e427477f2873b5963996f5272fadd75cdf79065e627cc3eb | Business, ownership, governance, transaction package, litigation, corrections to CP-0 and CP-1 |
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Creditors look adequately protected in the near term but the credit is weakening: liquidity of USD 3,308 million covers 2027 maturities, while net asset value, income and covenant headroom are eroding. | Medium | Covenant definitions, the borrowing base, ratings and common stock ownership are not supplied, so headroom is a proxy and confidence stays at medium. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Net asset value per share fell from USD 20.89 to USD 18.28 over nine months 2026 while debt principal fell to USD 6,337 million. | Deleveraging by asset sales left debt at 126.8% of common equity, so protection depends on portfolio marks. | High |

| Liquidity of USD 3,308 million compares with USD 900 million of 2027 maturities and USD 3,944 million due in 2029 to 2031. | Near-term refinancing is covered; the larger test is the 2029 to 2031 wall and the cost of new notes. | Medium |

| The revolver equity floor of USD 3,750.0 million is the nearest covenant constraint, about 11.0% of investment fair value away. | Equity-based tests tighten before the asset coverage test, so further marks matter more than leverage ratios. | Medium |

| Net investment income covered 98.1% of common distributions over nine months and 95.0% in Q3 without the fee waiver. | Distributions compete with debt reduction, and the waiver ends after the quarter ending March 31, 2027. | Medium |

| USD 4,650 million of unsecured notes sit beside USD 1,687 million of secured debt and a revolver with USD 3,134 million available. | Secured capacity can rank ahead of the notes; sponsor support of USD 150 million is small against the USD 850 million equity decline. | Medium |
### Credit view

FS KKR Capital Corp's creditors are adequately protected in the near term, but the credit is weakening because the equity value beneath the debt is shrinking. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 3,308 million against USD 900 million of notes maturing in 2027, asset coverage of 179% on debt against the 150% minimum, and a lender-agreed lower equity floor of USD 3,750.0 million. The weakest point is the fall in net asset value per share from USD 20.89 to USD 18.28 over nine months 2026, with investment income down 24.2% as the portfolio shrinks, distributions above net investment income and five stockholder suits with no loss estimate. What decides the outcome is whether portfolio marks stabilise and non-accruals, at 3.4% of fair value, keep falling, because the covenants and the asset coverage test all run off net asset value. [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 figures; CP-1A governance and litigation rows]
### Key findings

The equity cushion under the debt is eroding even as debt falls. Over nine months 2026 common equity fell by USD 850 million to USD 4,999 million, net asset value per share fell from USD 20.89 to USD 18.28, and realised and unrealised losses of USD 766 million outran net investment income of USD 366 million, while debt principal fell 16.8% to USD 6,337 million. Because the debt reduction came from asset sales and repayments rather than retained earnings, debt principal to common equity eased only from 130.3% to 126.8%, so creditors still depend on portfolio marks to hold the cushion. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 Financials and credit metrics and Calculations]

Liquidity is adequate for the next two years but the later wall is larger. The issuer holds USD 111 million of cash and USD 3,197 million of availability, subject to a borrowing base that is not printed, which is 3.68 times the USD 900 million of notes due in January and July 2027 and 2.14 times unfunded commitments of USD 1,545.4 million. No committed facility expires within twelve months. Maturities then rise to USD 1,000 million in 2029, USD 1,644 million in 2030 and USD 1,300 million in 2031, USD 3,944 million in total or 62.2% of principal debt, and the 7.500% coupon on the USD 900 million of 2031 notes issued on June 8, 2026 compares with 3.400% on the notes that reached maturity in January 2026, so refinancing will cost more. [Documentary Fact for the schedule; Analyst Interpretation for the wall; CP-1 debt maturities; CP-1A transaction summary]

The nearest covenant constraint is the equity floor, not the leverage ratio. On May 8, 2026 lenders agreed to cut revolver commitments to about USD 4,051.7 million from USD 4,700.0 million, raise margins and reset the minimum shareholders' equity floor to USD 3,750.0 million from about USD 5,048.6 million. Common equity of USD 4,999 million is USD 1,249.0 million, or 25.0%, above the new floor on a proxy basis, which equals a fall of about 11.0% in investment fair value; asset coverage would take roughly a 15% to 16% fall in its base to reach 150%. Equity at 2026-09-30 was USD 49.6 million below the former floor, so, on this proxy, the amendment avoided a breach. The credit agreement's definition of equity is not supplied, so this ordering is an interpretation. [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Covenants and headroom]

Earnings no longer cover the shareholder distribution without sponsor support. Investment income fell 21.2% in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 and net investment income was USD 127 million, after a USD 12 million incentive fee waiver that runs to the quarter ending March 31, 2027 with no recoupment. Net investment income covered 105.0% of Q3 common distributions of USD 121 million with the waiver and 95.0% without it, and 98.1% over nine months, while a special distribution of USD 0.20 per share and a regular USD 0.44 were declared for the fourth quarter. When the waiver ends, the same income would leave distributions about USD 12 million a quarter less covered, so either the distribution, the portfolio size or net asset value must give; each reduces the cushion or the cash available to reduce debt. [Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the consequence; CP-1 Earnings and income quality; CP-1A fee waiver row]

The debt structure puts the unsecured notes behind secured claims that can grow. The issuer has USD 4,650 million of unsecured notes against USD 1,687 million of secured debt, 73.4% and 26.6% of principal debt. The revolver is secured on substantially all assets of the Company and certain subsidiaries and has USD 3,134 million of availability, so secured borrowing ahead of the notes can rise subject to the borrowing base and the 150% asset coverage test; the 7.500% notes state they rank effectively junior to secured debt and are structurally junior to subsidiary debt. As a balance sheet mechanic and not a recovery estimate, investments at fair value less secured debt are 2.07 times the unsecured notes today. The joint venture, worth 32.7% of common equity, also carries USD 2,330.9 million of its own debt that ranks ahead of the issuer in its assets. [Documentary Fact for the structure; Analyst Interpretation for the mechanics; CP-1 Debt schedule; CP-1A Company and operating model]

Sponsor support is real but small against the decline, and governance carries open items. A KKR affiliate paid USD 150 million for convertible preferred stock that ranks junior to debt, a KKR subsidiary ran a tender offer, and the adviser waived half its subordinated income incentive fee, but the USD 150 million is 17.6% of the USD 850 million fall in equity and the preferred carries two board seats, a change-of-control put and a holder put after six years. Share repurchases of USD 90 million through October 30, 2026 use the same cash that could reduce debt. Five stockholder suits allege misleading statements on valuations and distributions, two challenge adviser fees, and the Company states it cannot estimate a loss. No priming, uptiering, collateral release or non-pro-rata exchange is documented, but the executed agreements are not supplied, so legal capacity for such steps is not assessed. [Documentary Fact for the actions; Analyst Interpretation for the weighting; CP-1A governance, ownership and conflicts rows]
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Liquidity and maturity profile: USD 3,308 million of cash plus availability, no committed facility expiring within twelve months and USD 900 million due in 2027, so near-term debt service and refinancing are covered unless the borrowing base falls sharply. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 liquidity and maturities]. Loan book quality and seniority: 63.2% senior secured across 234 portfolio companies, top ten exposure of 21%, a 10.0% yield on accruing debt and non-accruals down from 4.2% to 3.4% of fair value since March 31, 2026, which supports interest income and marks. [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model; CP-1 Financials]. Statutory and covenant headroom with lender support: asset coverage of 179% on debt against a 150% minimum, a lender-agreed lower equity floor and compliance reported at 2026-09-30, which show lenders willing to adjust terms rather than restrict the facility. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the lender reading; CP-1 Covenants]. Sponsor alignment: preferred capital, a tender, a four-quarter fee waiver with no recoupment and an adviser jointly run by KKR Credit and Future Standard give creditors an engaged sponsor, though the support is limited in size. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A governance rows]. Rate balance: a 100 basis point rise adds USD 27 million to twelve-month net interest income and a fall removes the same, with USD 2,600 million of fixed-rate notes swapped to floating, so rate moves do not threaten debt service on their own. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 debt schedule and earnings notes].

Weaknesses. Shrinking cushion and income: net asset value per share is down 12.5% over nine months, investment income is down 24.2%, and debt principal is still 126.8% of common equity, so the earnings base and the cushion both shrink together. [Documentary Fact; CP-1 Calculations]. Distribution not covered without help: net investment income covered 98.1% of nine-month common distributions and would cover 95.0% in Q3 without the waiver, which ends after the quarter ending March 31, 2027; a special distribution and share repurchases continue. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 and CP-1A]. Equity-based covenant is the nearest limit: the USD 3,750.0 million floor is about 11.0% of investment fair value from current equity and its definition is not supplied. [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Covenants]. Concentration in affiliated and structured holdings: the joint venture is 32.7% of common equity with USD 2,330.9 million of its own debt, asset based finance is 11.6% and equity and other 9.9% of fair value, and affiliated dividend income was USD 84 million of Q3 income of USD 294 million. [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Company and operating model]. Unsecured ranking and growing secured capacity: USD 4,650 million of notes rank effectively junior to USD 1,687 million of secured debt plus up to USD 3,134 million of revolver availability. [Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 Debt schedule]. Legal and valuation scrutiny: five suits about valuations and distributions with no loss estimate, in a business where reported net asset value drives every test. [Documentary Fact; CP-1A Claims and governance rows]. Disclosure limits: no ratings, no common stock ownership table, no covenant certificate and no quantified target leverage, so monitoring relies on management statements. [Insufficient Information; CP-0 and CP-1A gaps].
### Credit assessment
| Element | Content | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Adequate near-term protection with a weakening trend; equity-based tests and net asset value are the swing factors | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 liquidity, maturities, covenants and earnings; CP-1A governance, transaction and litigation rows |

| Thesis | FS KKR Capital Corp has the liquidity and asset seniority to meet its 2027 debt, but shrinking net asset value, uncovered distributions and unsecured ranking mean creditor protection depends on stable portfolio marks and continued sponsor and lender support | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | As above |

| Confidence cap | Below High because the CP-1A readiness judgment of this module is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and covenant definitions, borrowing base, ratings and ownership are not supplied | Insufficient Information | Not applicable | CP-1A Consumers table; CP-1 Gaps |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Further net asset value decline | Equity of USD 4,999 million is USD 1,249.0 million above the floor; non-accrual, spread widening or joint venture marks reduce it | Covenant relief would be needed again; margin and commitment concessions accompanied the last one | Material |

| Distribution and buyback pressure | Net investment income covered 98.1% of nine-month distributions; the waiver ends after the quarter ending March 31, 2027 | Cash to equity competes with debt reduction; a cut would signal weaker income | Material |

| Secured capacity ahead of notes | The revolver is secured and has USD 3,134 million available; the notes are effectively junior | Dilution of unsecured claims if the revolver is drawn, limited by the borrowing base and asset coverage test | Material |
| Refinancing cost and 2029 to 2031 wall | USD 3,944 million matures in 2029 to 2031; new notes priced at 7.500% | Higher interest expense against a shrinking income base | Material |

| Joint venture and affiliated concentration | Joint venture equals 32.7% of common equity and has its own senior debt of USD 2,330.9 million | Equity and coverage sensitive to one holding and to its lenders ranking first | Material |

| Litigation and valuation credibility | Five suits allege misstatements about valuations and distributions; no loss estimate | Contingent claim and potential effect on reported net asset value | Minor to Material, unquantified |
| Disclosure and legal capacity gaps | Executed agreements, ownership and covenant certificates not supplied | Priming or asset transfer capacity cannot be assessed | Minor |
### Corrections and consistency

The earlier handoffs agree on the figures used here. Two corrections already stated in CP-1A govern this module: the share of affiliated dividend income attributable to the joint venture is not supplied (CP-1 had said it was included), and the CCT Tokyo facility was terminated on June 29, 2026 rather than lapsing at its listed maturity. CP-0's statement that covenant levels were not printed is superseded by CP-1: the revolver equity floor is USD 3,750.0 million.
## Calculations
All inputs are figures in the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs.
| Calculation | Inputs | Result |
| Liquidity to 2027 maturities | 3,308 / 900 | 3.68 times |
| Liquidity to unfunded commitments | 3,308 / 1,545.4 | 2.14 times (CP-1) |
| 2027 maturities as share of principal debt | 900 / 6,337 | 14.2% |
| 2029 to 2031 maturities | 1,000 + 1,644 + 1,300; 3,944 / 6,337 | USD 3,944 million, 62.2% of principal debt |
| Equity floor headroom against investment fair value | 1,249.0 / 11,306 | 11.0% |
| Asset coverage fall to 150% | 1 - 1.50 / 1.77; 1 - 1.50 / 1.79 (CP-1) | about 15.3% including preferred and 16.2% on debt only, from rounded ratios |
| Unsecured notes balance sheet cover | (11,306 - 1,687) / 4,650 = 9,619 / 4,650 | 2.07 times; a mechanic using fair value of investments and ignoring other liabilities, not a recovery estimate |
| Net investment income to common distributions, nine months | 366 / 373 | 98.1% |
| Net investment income to common distributions, Q3 | 127 / 121; (127 - 12) / 121 | 105.0%; 95.0% without the waiver |
| Sponsor preferred against equity decline | 150 / 850 | 17.6% |
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | What it affects | Action |

| Credit agreement definition of shareholders' equity, compliance certificate and borrowing base not supplied | Material | Covenant headroom and availability, hence liquidity | Treat headroom as a proxy and availability as base-limited; request the certificate if covenant analysis is needed |
| No ratings, market debt quotes or peers | Material | External view of the credit and market access | Not supplied; do not infer |
| Common stock ownership, tender offer result and executed agreements not supplied | Minor | Sponsor alignment and legal capacity | Keep Insufficient Information rows |
| Loss from five stockholder suits not estimable; no accrual shown | Material | Contingent claim and reported net asset value | Monitor court developments |
| Target leverage range not quantified; use of proceeds of the 2031 notes not stated | Minor | Management intent | Treat as Management Language |
| Joint venture full statements and look-through not supplied | Minor | Concentration and valuation risk | Use selected data only |
| CP-1A readiness for this module is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS, not READY | Inherited | Confidence is capped below High | Restated in the Credit assessment table |
## Next module

CP-5 (evidence trace validator) should test each material claim above against the cited CP-1 and CP-1A rows and the pinned sources, in particular: the equity floor figures of USD 3,750.0 million and about USD 5,048.6 million, the liquidity and maturity figures, the 98.1% and 95.0% coverage ratios, the secured and unsecured split, the joint venture figures, and the count of five stockholder suits. It should also check the figures that CP-1A and this module labelled as calculated, and confirm that no recovery, peer or instrument conclusion appears.
